title: Jabez asked for more.
paragraphs: Jabez asked for more.

Not safety.
Not survival.
More.
And heaven did not rebuke him.
Read that again.

In a world that teaches people to shrink back, apologize for hunger, and expect little from God, Jabez dared to pray a dangerous prayer:
“Oh, that You would bless me indeed, and enlarge my territory…”
And God answered him.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

Jabez was not just asking for land.
He was asking for impact.
Not just increase.
Stewardship.
Not just more space around him.
More room for God’s hand upon him.
That changes everything.

Because bold prayer is not arrogance when it bows before God.
It is faith.
And maybe that is the part people miss.

Jabez did not demand a throne.
He asked for blessing.
He asked for God’s hand.
He asked for protection from evil.
He asked that sorrow would not define him.
This is where the story gets personal.

Some of you have been taught to live beneath what God is calling you into.
You pray small because you feel small.
You ask cautiously because pain has discipled you more than truth.
You whisper requests as if God is irritated by your need.

But Scripture does not show a bothered Savior.
It shows a generous God.

Still, the deeper issue is not just whether God will enlarge your territory.
It is whether your heart has been surrendered to Him.
Because outside of Christ, even answered prayers cannot save a soul.

Sin is still the real problem.
Not limitation.
Not delay.
Not lack.

Sin separates us from God.
Pride blinds us.
Self-rule destroys us.
And no amount of influence, provision, or open doors can heal what only Jesus can redeem.
That is why the Gospel is everything.

Jesus Christ came for sinners.
He lived the holy life we failed to live.
He died on the cross for our sin.
He rose again in victory.
And now through repentance and faith in Him, we are not merely given “more.”
We are given mercy.
We are given new life.
We are given God Himself.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior, this truth is deeper than a single post can hold.
Start here:
So yes—pray boldly.

Ask God to enlarge what He wants to use.
Ask Him to put His hand on your life.
Ask Him to guard you from evil.
Ask Him to make your life count for His glory.
But do not stop there.
Ask for the greater miracle.

Ask for a clean heart.
Ask for repentance.
Ask for faith in Jesus Christ.
Ask for the grace that only the cross can give.
Because the boldest prayer is not “Lord, give me more.”

It is:
“Lord Jesus, save me. Rule me. Use me.”
If this found you, it’s not by accident. And the source matters.

But here’s what most people don’t realize…
God is not glorified by timid faith dressed up as humility.
He is glorified when broken people trust Him enough to ask, surrender, repent, and believe.
So here is the question:

Are you asking God for bigger territory—
while refusing to give Jesus your whole heart?
